questions.enonce_markdown: Two events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A) = \tfrac{3}{10}$ and $P(A \cup B) = \tfrac45$. Find $P(B)$ if $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive.
questions.corrige_markdown:
If $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, $P(A \cap B) = 0$, so the addition rule reduces to $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B)$:

$$P(B) = \frac45 - \frac{3}{10} = \frac{8}{10} - \frac{3}{10} = \frac12$$

**$P(B) = \dfrac12$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A) = \tfrac{3}{10}$ and $P(A \cup B) = \tfrac45$. Find $P(B)$ if $A$ and $B$ are independent.
questions.corrige_markdown:
If $A$ and $B$ are independent, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B)$. The addition rule $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$ gives

$$\frac45 = \frac{3}{10} + P(B) - \frac{3}{10}P(B) = \frac{3}{10} + \frac{7}{10}P(B)$$

$$\frac{7}{10}P(B) = \frac45 - \frac{3}{10} = \frac12 \;\Rightarrow\; P(B) = \frac12\times\frac{10}{7} = \frac57$$

(Check: $P(A \cap B) = \tfrac{3}{10}\times\tfrac57 = \tfrac{3}{14}$ and $P(A \cup B) = \tfrac{3}{10} + \tfrac57 - \tfrac{3}{14} = \tfrac{21 + 50 - 15}{70} = \tfrac{56}{70} = \tfrac45$.)

**$P(B) = \dfrac57$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Bag $X$ contains $7$ balls, of which $2$ are red, $4$ are green and $1$ is blue. Bag $Y$ contains $6$ balls, of which $1$ is red, $2$ are green and $3$ are blue. A biased die is thrown and the probability of obtaining an even score is $\tfrac35$. If the score on the die is even, Bag $X$ is chosen, otherwise Bag $Y$ is chosen. A ball is selected at random from a bag. Draw a tree diagram showing all the possible outcomes.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Probabilities of the first stage.** $P(\text{even}) = \tfrac35$ (Bag $X$ chosen) and $P(\text{odd}) = 1 - \tfrac35 = \tfrac25$ (Bag $Y$ chosen).

**Second stage.** Bag $X$ ($7$ balls): $P(R) = \tfrac27$, $P(G) = \tfrac47$, $P(B) = \tfrac17$. Bag $Y$ ($6$ balls): $P(R) = \tfrac16$, $P(G) = \tfrac26 = \tfrac13$, $P(B) = \tfrac36 = \tfrac12$. (R = red, G = green, B = blue ball; each set of branches sums to $1$.)

**Tree diagram** (branch probabilities on the branches, outcome probabilities on the right):

```
                 2/7 ---- Red   : 3/5 x 2/7 = 6/35
        3/5     /
  Bag X ------- 4/7 ---- Green : 3/5 x 4/7 = 12/35
     /          \
    /            1/7 ---- Blue  : 3/5 x 1/7 = 3/35
 Start
    \            1/6 ---- Red   : 2/5 x 1/6 = 1/15
     \          /
  Bag Y ------- 1/3 ---- Green : 2/5 x 1/3 = 2/15
        2/5     \
                 1/2 ---- Blue  : 2/5 x 1/2 = 1/5
```

| Bag | Ball | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| $X$ (even, $\tfrac35$) | red | $\tfrac35\times\tfrac27 = \tfrac{6}{35}$ |
| $X$ | green | $\tfrac35\times\tfrac47 = \tfrac{12}{35}$ |
| $X$ | blue | $\tfrac35\times\tfrac17 = \tfrac{3}{35}$ |
| $Y$ (odd, $\tfrac25$) | red | $\tfrac25\times\tfrac16 = \tfrac{1}{15}$ |
| $Y$ | green | $\tfrac25\times\tfrac13 = \tfrac{2}{15}$ |
| $Y$ | blue | $\tfrac25\times\tfrac12 = \tfrac15$ |

(Check: $\tfrac{6 + 12 + 3}{35} + \tfrac{1 + 2 + 3}{15} = \tfrac35 + \tfrac25 = 1$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Bag $X$ contains $7$ balls, of which $2$ are red, $4$ are green and $1$ is blue. Bag $Y$ contains $6$ balls, of which $1$ is red, $2$ are green and $3$ are blue. A biased die is thrown and the probability of obtaining an even score is $\tfrac35$. If the score on the die is even, Bag $X$ is chosen, otherwise Bag $Y$ is chosen. A ball is selected at random from a bag. Hence, find the probability that the ball is red.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A red ball comes either from Bag $X$ or from Bag $Y$ (mutually exclusive routes), so add the two branch products of the tree:

$$P(\text{red}) = \frac35\times\frac27 + \frac25\times\frac16 = \frac{6}{35} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{18}{105} + \frac{7}{105} = \frac{25}{105} = \frac{5}{21}$$

**$P(\text{red}) = \dfrac{5}{21} \approx 0.238$.**

Bag $X$ contains $7$ balls, of which $2$ are red, $4$ are green and $1$ is blue. Bag $Y$ contains $6$ balls, of which $1$ is red, $2$ are green and $3$ are blue. A biased die is thrown and the probability of obtaining an even score is $\tfrac35$. If the score on the die is even, Bag $X$ is chosen, otherwise Bag $Y$ is chosen. A ball is selected at random from a bag. Given that the ball is blue, find the probability that it is from Bag $Y$. [This last part has no printed label; numbered (f) here.]
questions.corrige_markdown:
This is a conditional probability: $P(Y \mid \text{blue}) = \dfrac{P(Y \cap \text{blue})}{P(\text{blue})}$.

From the tree: $P(Y \cap \text{blue}) = \tfrac25\times\tfrac12 = \tfrac15$ and

$$P(\text{blue}) = \frac35\times\frac17 + \frac25\times\frac12 = \frac{3}{35} + \frac{7}{35} = \frac{10}{35} = \frac27$$

(Check: $P(\text{red}) + P(\text{green}) + P(\text{blue}) = \tfrac{25 + 50 + 30}{105} = 1$.)

$$P(Y \mid \text{blue}) = \frac{1/5}{2/7} = \frac15\times\frac72 = \frac{7}{10}$$

**$P(\text{Bag } Y \mid \text{blue}) = \dfrac{7}{10}$.**
